steps.saw: A name, "Nimay Parekh", a quote, "My agents have a policy. Do yours?", and a wordmark "RISK MANDATE". Blue stripe on the left. No title, no email, no one-line description of the company.
steps.thought: I do not remember this person. The quote suggests something in AI agent governance or policy, which is a category I am actively looking at, but it is a provocation, not a description. I cannot tell if RiskMandate is a company, a product, a consultancy or a slogan. No role either, so I do not know if he is a founder or a salesperson.
steps.question: What does RiskMandate actually sell, and who is Nimay in it?
steps.confusion: I had to guess the category from a rhetorical question. "Policy" could mean insurance, compliance or access control.
steps.reason: The front gives me a category hint but no category line. I give each card one turn before deciding.

steps.saw: A QR code, three lines: "Meet me", "Book a meeting", "Talk to my agent", and a URL "web-summit.sgit.ai /meet/nimay/".
steps.thought: Three calls to action and still no sentence about the company. The domain is sgit.ai, not riskmandate-anything, which makes me wonder whether RiskMandate is a company or a project inside something called SGit. "Talk to my agent" is on theme. Scanning costs me five seconds, and AI agent governance is relevant to my thesis, so I will give it one look.
steps.question: Why is the URL on a web-summit.sgit.ai domain and not a RiskMandate domain?
steps.confusion: Unclear relationship between SGit and RiskMandate. I could not tell which one is the company.
steps.action: Scanned the QR with my iPhone camera.
steps.reason: Relevant category, and the scan is cheaper than deciding without information. I would not have typed the URL.

steps.saw: A site header "web-summit.sgit.ai", a version badge "v0.2.265", two rows of navigation (Start, Team, Work, Summit, PKI, About, then People, The map, Setup, Everything, The cast, Briefs, Pulse, Agents, At work, ABPs, Meet us), a "Who are you?" dropdown, and a large box: "Add your key. Your conductor agent gives you a key... Paste my key / Choose the file". At the very bottom, a breadcrumb ending "Meet Nimay Parekh".
steps.thought: This looks like an internal team tool, not a page for someone who received a card. I do not have a conductor agent and I do not have a key. My first instinct was that the QR was wrong. Only the breadcrumb told me I was on the right page.
steps.question: Am I supposed to have a key? Is this page meant for me at all?
steps.confusion: The whole first screen is addressed to team members. "Conductor agent", "sealed to you", "ABPs" mean nothing to me. A version number on a sales page is odd.
steps.reason: The breadcrumb said "Meet Nimay Parekh", so I gave it one swipe. Had the breadcrumb not been there I would have closed the tab.

steps.saw: "Meet Nimay Parekh. Hello, and thanks for scanning. You met Nimay Parekh, from the RiskMandate team at Web Summit Lisbon, 9 to 12 November 2026." Then "RiskMandate, in short. Know their reach. Define their mandate. Control the gap. AI agents now act for companies. RiskMandate gives each one a factual record teams can check: its Reach..., its Mandate..., the Gap between them, and the real Barriers, with a Licence to Operate..." and three questions about agents.
steps.thought: Now I have it. Agent governance: inventory what an AI agent can touch versus what it was authorised to do, and record accountability. That is a real category and a timely one; I can see buyers in security and risk teams. This paragraph should have been the first thing I saw, and a shorter version of it should be on the card. Still missing: is this a company, what stage, who are the founders, is there a product or only a framework, is it raising.
steps.question: Is there a product with customers, or is this a framework? Is RiskMandate a company that is raising?
steps.confusion: "Licence to Operate" and "Barriers" read like framework vocabulary. I could not tell if this is software, a standard or a consulting method.
steps.action: Scrolled to see how to reach him.
steps.reason: The category passed my first filter. Now I need a contact route and some sign of a company behind it.

steps.saw: "Talk to us. Book a meeting with Nimay: the booking link is coming this week. Until then, find us at our stand on Thursday 12 November. Talk to Nimay's agent: coming this week. See how we work: this whole site is run in the open by seven people and their agents." Footer: "Built and run by an AI agent with a named human operator.", "v0.2.265", "GitHub", license lines, and a grey block "For an agent: this page is...".
steps.thought: Two of the three promises on the back of the card are "coming this week". There is no email address, no LinkedIn, no company site. The only route is a stand on the last day, and I may not be there. "Seven people and their agents" and a GitHub link suggest something closer to an open project than a funded startup. Interesting, honestly, but I cannot see a company I could invest in from this page.
steps.question: How do I contact Nimay tonight, by email, without waiting for a booking link?
steps.confusion: The card says "Book a meeting" and the page says the booking link does not exist yet. The stand location is not given, only the day.
steps.reason: Checking whether there is an email or anything else at the bottom.

steps.saw: The end of the grey agent block, "summit.sgit.ai/agent/index.html.", and blank space.
steps.thought: Nothing else. No contact details. The page ends with instructions for a machine, not for me.
steps.confusion: I do not know why a meet page ends with text addressed to an agent.
steps.action: Closed the tab and put the card in my "maybe, category interesting" pile rather than "follow up".
steps.reason: Good category, but no stage, no founder signal and no way to write to him. I will not hunt for the person.

steps.saw: Seven cards with identical layout: Dinis Cruz "Ask me what my agents did today.", Nimay Parekh "My agents have a policy. Do yours?", Angelo "Ask me how I control my agents.", Jose Bota "I brought 6 agents. Ask me why.", Vicky "Who's on the other side of your agent?", Silvio Switha "Agents with a mandate.", Indi Gupte "Your agents. Your rules." Each in a different colour, all "RISK MANDATE".
steps.thought: Seven cards, one company. That is actually the strongest signal of the evening: there is a team, at least seven people, working the event in a coordinated way. Read together the quotes add up to the category, which no single card did. But none of them says what RiskMandate is, and none names a founder or a role. I still cannot tell who to email.
steps.question: Who is the CEO or founder among these seven?
steps.confusion: Two cards have first names only (Angelo, Vicky). I could not tell which person is senior.
steps.action: Clipped the seven together and kept them in the maybe pile, with a note: agent governance, Lisbon, check stand Thursday.
steps.reason: The team signal moved it up slightly, but without a contact or a stage I will not chase it.

interview.q1: It gives companies a checkable record of what each AI agent can reach versus what it was authorised to do, and who is accountable for the gap, though I only learned that on the second phone screen.
interview.q2: Nothing tonight. If I pass the stand on Thursday I will stop; otherwise the cards stay in the maybe pile and I will likely not follow up, because there is no email to write to.
interview.q3: A one-line category on the card itself, Nimay's role, a company website or email, and any signal of stage: founded when, customers, raising or not. The booking link and the agent were both missing too.
interview.q4: Partly. The category explanation is precise and sober, and seven coordinated cards suggest a real team. But the page opens with an internal key login, shows a version number, says it is run by an AI agent, and two of three promised actions are not live yet. That reads as a project in progress, not a company I can diligence.
interview.q5: Jose Bota's, "I brought 6 agents. Ask me why.", because it has a number and a reason to talk. Silvio's "Agents with a mandate." is the closest to a category line. Nimay's I remember only because I scanned it.
interview.q6: Put one plain sentence on the back, such as "RiskMandate: governance records for AI agents", and make the QR page open on that sentence with Nimay's email, not on a key box.

findings.what: The front has no category line; the company's purpose must be inferred from a rhetorical question.
Nimay's role is not stated on the card, so an investor cannot tell founder from staff.
The back offers three actions but still no sentence saying what RiskMandate does.
The URL is on web-summit.sgit.ai, which blurs whether RiskMandate or SGit is the company.
The QR scans cleanly to the right page and the scan is cheap enough to try.
The first phone screen is an internal "Add your key" box and two rows of team navigation; a card recipient nearly closed the tab. Only the breadcrumb "Meet Nimay Parekh" kept her.
The "RiskMandate, in short" paragraph is a clear, credible category explanation, but it sits below the fold.
"Book a meeting" and "Talk to my agent" are both "coming this week"; there is no email or other contact route, and the stand location is not given.
No stage, funding, customer or founder signal anywhere on the page, which is what an investor needs to decide on a follow-up.
The footer "Built and run by an AI agent", the version number and the agent block read as an open project rather than a company.
Seven matching cards signal a real, coordinated team, and together the quotes explain the category better than any one card.
In the stack no card names a founder or senior person, and two carry first names only, so she cannot tell whom to contact.
